title: Jad root setting.json
description: Workspace-level session roots used by the web UI session list.

server.description: Local HTTP server defaults. Explicit server options and environment variables override these values.

host.description: Address the server listens on; HOST overrides it. With server.remote_api enabled and no listen_unix it must name one address, never a wildcard such as 0.0.0.0 or ::, because the bearer token of a remote then answers there in clear text.

run_state_retention_ms.description: How long a finished run stays attachable, so a browser reload can still catch its completion.

tool_stream_interval_ms.description: Coalescing window for in-progress tool-call snapshots. Long arguments stream as one snapshot per window instead of one per delta; 0 streams every delta.

run_content_memory_bytes.description: Maximum in-memory UTF-8 bytes retained for the active output item's content before concatenated content spills to one responses.partial file in the response-turn staging directory. 0 spills any non-empty content immediately.

run_content_fallback_max_bytes.description: Go backend only. Cap on the in-memory copy of the streamed answer text that the run keeps when its responses.partial file cannot be created or written (disk full, read-only state directory). Past the cap the copy stops growing: a client that attaches late sees the first bytes followed by a truncation marker, and the server logs a warning. Clients already attached and the committed transcript are not affected.

run_content_write_batch_bytes.description: Target UTF-8 content bytes per asynchronous append to responses.partial. Buffered content remains bounded by run_content_memory_bytes (with encoded-buffer overhead).

run_content_flush_interval_ms.description: Maximum delay before flushing a partial content append batch. 0 schedules immediate asynchronous flushing.

run_content_max_index_segments.description: Maximum item-range/contribution segments per active response before the writer compacts redundant ranges or the cache uses a correctness-first fallback.

sse_max_buffered_bytes.description: Maximum queued SSE response bytes per subscriber before the connection closes and can be reattached to a current snapshot.

sse_heartbeat_interval_ms.description: Gap between keep-alive frames on a run stream that has nothing else to send, such as during a long tool call. Keeps the browser from treating a quiet connection as dead. Keep it well below the browser's stall timeout. 0 disables the frames.

sse_write_timeout_ms.description: Go backend only. How long one write to a run stream (an event or a keep-alive frame) may take. A client that does not read for this long is disconnected and its queue released; it can reattach to a current snapshot. The deadline is renewed before every write, so a healthy long stream is not cut. 0 disables the limit.

read_header_timeout_ms.description: Time a client has to send complete request headers before the connection is closed. Bounds slow-header clients. 0 disables the limit. There is deliberately no whole-request or response timeout, which would cut long-lived SSE run streams.

idle_timeout_ms.description: Time an idle keep-alive connection stays open between requests before it is closed. 0 disables the limit.

shutdown_timeout_ms.description: Go backend only. How long the server waits for in-flight requests to finish after SIGINT or SIGTERM, once active runs are cancelled. When it runs out, the remaining connections are closed and the server exits. 0 waits without a limit.

session_delete_stop_wait_ms.description: Go backend only. How long deleting a session waits for its stopped runs to end before the delete is refused with a conflict. 0 does not wait, so a session with an active run is refused at once.

session_store_idle_ms.description: Go backend only. How long a session's transcript store (its run lock, runner and transcript indexes) stays in memory after the last request that used it ends. A later request opens it again from disk, with the same recovery as the first open after a start. 0 keeps every store until the session is deleted or the server stops.

log_level.description: Go backend only. Minimum level of the structured server log. debug adds one access-log line per request (method, route template, status, duration, bytes); off disables logging. The TypeScript backend ignores this key.

log_format.description: Go backend only. Log line encoding: key=value text or one JSON object per line. The TypeScript backend ignores this key.

log_file.description: Go backend only. Append the server log to this file instead of standard error; a relative path is resolved against the directory of this setting file, the file is created with mode 0600, and the Go backend refuses to start when it cannot be opened. There is no rotation. Empty or absent logs to standard error. The TypeScript backend ignores this key.

recover_processes_at_start.description: Go backend only. At start, in the background, recover the managed-process storage of every session and path profile that configures the process tool: a process a crashed server left running is stopped (see tools.native.process.stop_orphans) and its manifest marked lost, instead of waiting for the first use of the process tool in that session. Only storage directories that already exist are visited. false keeps the recovery lazy. The TypeScript backend ignores this key.

recover_subagent_runs_at_start.description: Go backend only. At start, in the background, load the sub-agent run manifests of every session and path profile whose tools.native.subagent.persist_runs is on and whose storage directory exists: a run the last server left queued or running is marked lost, and the oldest ended runs beyond keep_finished are dropped (with delete_transcripts, their transcript folders are deleted), instead of waiting for the first use of the subagent tool in that session. A run of another server that is still running on the same directory is left alone. false keeps the recovery lazy. The TypeScript backend ignores this key.

conditional_requests.description: Answer session list and snapshot requests with 304 when the state they were built from is unchanged.

snapshot_turns.description: Newest turns included in a session snapshot; older ones are paged. 0 returns the whole transcript.

max_page_turns.description: Largest number of turns one cursor page may return.

max_inline_part_bytes.description: Inline text kept per transcript part, in bytes. A larger part is cut for transport, reports its full size, and is re-fetched whole through the message endpoint; 0 sends parts uncut.

max_request_images.description: Go backend only. The most images one run request may carry in an array input ({"type":"image","data":<base64 or data URL>}). 0 refuses image input. The TypeScript backend ignores this key.

max_request_image_bytes.description: Go backend only. The largest decoded image of a run request, in bytes. The run request may carry the base64 text of up to max_request_images images on top of max_body_bytes (the rest of the body must still fit in max_body_bytes). The TypeScript backend ignores this key.

max_request_files.description: Go backend only. The most files one run request may carry in an array input ({"type":"file","name":<file name>,"data":<base64 or data URL>}). Only PDF files are accepted, judged by their first bytes. 0 refuses file input. The TypeScript backend ignores this key.

max_concurrent_runs.description: Go backend only. The most runs that may be running at the same time across all sessions. A run start beyond it is refused with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After of 5 seconds, and nothing is changed. 0 means no cap. Runs of sub-agents are not counted; they are part of their parent run. Nested profile_message runs are not counted either.

max_leaf_calls.description: Go backend only. The most leaf tool calls (bash, edit, notebook, lsp, write, read, grep, glob, fetch, read_image) that may run at once in the whole process, across every session and sub-agent. A leaf call waits for a free slot; nothing is refused. Wrapper, MCP and other tools are not counted.

max_request_file_bytes.description: Go backend only. The largest decoded file of a run request, in bytes. The run request may carry the base64 text of up to max_request_files files on top of max_body_bytes (the rest of the body must still fit in max_body_bytes). A file is kept whole in messages.jsonl and sent again with every later request. The TypeScript backend ignores this key.

allowed_origins.description: Exact browser origins permitted to call the API; configure the frontend dev-server origin when using its proxy. The server also requires JAD_API_TOKEN in the environment.

tracing.description: Go backend only. OpenTelemetry spans for every run (jad.run), model request (chat <model>) and tool call (execute_tool <name>), exported over OTLP/HTTP (protobuf) by the server, `jad run` and `jad eval`. Attributes follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions (gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.tool.name, ...) plus jad.session, jad.profile, jad.turn_id and jad.round. Spans never carry prompts, answers, tool arguments, tool output or error text. Headers (for example an API key of a hosted collector) come from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS. Off by default; a change applies after a restart.

endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP base URL, for example http://127.0.0.1:4318; spans are sent to <endpoint>/v1/traces. Absent uses OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, else http://localhost:4318.

sample_ratio.description: Share of runs whose spans are recorded; a run's model requests and tool calls follow its decision.

export_timeout_ms.description: Time limit of one export request, and of the final flush when the process exits.

batch_timeout_ms.description: Longest time an ended span waits in the batch before it is exported.

max_queue_size.description: Ended spans kept for export; when the queue is full, new spans are dropped.

triggers.description: Go backend only. Runs the server starts by itself: on a cron schedule, or when a signed webhook arrives (a CI failure, a new issue). Each run goes through the same run route as the web client and `jad run`, so it takes the session's locks, is written to messages.jsonl and shows in the web client like any other turn; `jad run` and `jad eval` never run triggers. A trigger runs once at a time: while its previous run goes on, a new firing is recorded as skipped (a webhook gets 409). Webhooks: POST /api/triggers/<name> with the HMAC-SHA256 of the body (hex, with or without sha256=, the form GitHub sends) in signature_header; no API token, and nothing is accepted unsigned. GET /api/triggers (with the API token) lists the triggers, their next scheduled time, the run in progress and the last history_limit runs, newest first. The webhook body reaches the model as {payload}: it is text from outside, so treat a webhook trigger like a prompt anyone with the secret can write. Off by default; a change applies after a restart.

max_payload_bytes.description: Largest webhook body accepted; a larger one is refused with 413.

history_limit.description: Finished trigger runs kept in memory for GET /api/triggers; the oldest go first. The history is not kept across restarts.

signature_header.description: Header that carries the body's HMAC-SHA256.

notify.description: Places a finished trigger run is reported to, by name; a trigger lists the ones it uses in its notify. Each is an HTTP POST: format json sends the run as GET /api/triggers lists it plus text (one line: trigger, status, session, source, duration, cost) and, with answer_bytes, answer; format text sends that line, the error and the answer as text/plain, which ntfy-style services show as the message. A failed attempt (no answer, or a status outside 2xx) is retried; the outcome of each delivery is in the run's notifications in GET /api/triggers and a failure is logged. The address and the answer go to that service, so point it only at a service you trust with them. A change applies after a restart.

url.description: Absolute http or https address. Use url_env instead when the address itself is a secret (a Slack webhook, a private ntfy topic).

url_env.description: Environment variable that holds the address. The server does not start when it is unset, empty or not an http or https URL.

format.description: json: the run record with text and answer; text: plain text.

headers.description: Headers sent as written (for example Title or Tags for ntfy). Host and Content-Length are refused; Content-Type replaces the format's.

headers_env.description: Headers whose value is read from an environment variable, for a token (for example {"Authorization": "NTFY_AUTH"}, the variable holding "Bearer ..."). The server does not start when one is unset, empty or more than one line. A header may not be in both headers and headers_env.

on.description: Statuses that are reported. skipped (a firing while the previous run goes on) is left out by default, since a schedule that outruns its runs would report every firing.

retries.description: Attempts after a failed one. When the server stops, the attempt in progress ends and no retry starts.

answer_bytes.description: How much of the run's final answer is sent, cut on a character boundary; 0 sends none. The answer is model output and may repeat what tools read.

entries.description: Triggers by name; the name is the webhook path. Each needs a schedule, a webhook or both.

enabled.description: False keeps the entry in the file but leaves it out.

session.description: Session reference the run goes to (demo or root:demo).

profile.description: <category>/<name>; absent uses the session's default profile.

model.description: Model reference the profile allows; absent uses the profile's default.

prompt.description: The user message. {trigger} is the trigger's name, {time} the firing time (RFC 3339, UTC) and {payload} the webhook body (empty for a scheduled firing). Each is filled in once, so a placeholder inside the payload stays as it is.

schedule.description: Five-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week: *, numbers, a-b, */n, a-b/n, lists, 7 for Sunday) or @hourly, @daily, @midnight, @weekly, @monthly, @yearly, @annually. With both day fields restricted, either one matches, as in cron. Names (JAN, MON) are not accepted.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of schedule (for example Europe/Berlin or UTC); Local is the server's zone. Only with schedule. Needs the system's time zone data.

secret_env.description: Environment variable with the HMAC secret. The server does not start when it is unset or empty.

timeout_ms.description: Stops a run that has not ended after this long, as the stop button does; 0 leaves only the run's own limits (max_tool_rounds, max_run_tokens).

notify.description: Names in server.triggers.notify told when a run of this trigger ends; a name that is not there stops the server.

remote_api.description: Go backend only. Lets other JAD servers call profiles and sub-agents here (and read transcripts) under /api/remote/v1, with tokens from its own table, never the JAD_API_TOKEN. Off by default. Served on exactly one listener: listen_unix when it is set, which keeps the routes off the network, otherwise the main listener, which is plain http. The bearer token of a remote travels in clear text over TCP, so keep such a listener behind a VPN or on loopback, or set listen_unix. With it enabled and listen_unix empty, server.host (or HOST) must name one address, never a wildcard. A change applies after a restart; the token file is re-read on every change, so revoking a token is immediate.

tokens_file.description: JSON token table: {"tokens":[{"id":"build-box","sha256":"<64 hex of the token's SHA-256>","expires":"2026-12-31T00:00:00Z","revoked":false,"profiles":["main/review/*"],"agents":["main/review/*/explore"],"actions":["message","subagent","status","stop","transcripts","profile"],"max_hops":2}]}. profiles are globs over session/category/profile, agents over session/category/profile/agent ('*' does not cross '/'; [classes] are refused); a token with no glob reaches nothing. Only the hash is stored. The file must be mode 0600 (no group or other access) or the server refuses to start; it is re-read when its content or mode changes, checked at most every 250 ms. Relative to this file.

listen_unix.description: Absolute path of a unix socket to serve the remote routes on. The file is created with listen_unix_mode and removed at shutdown; a stale socket file is replaced, any other file at the path is an error.

listen_unix_mode.description: Permission bits of the socket as a decimal number (384 = 0600). Default 0600. A group or other write bit (0o022) is refused, so a mode such as 0664 or 0666 is an error.

max_hops.description: Most JAD servers a request may have passed through; a token's own max_hops can only lower it.

max_runs.description: Most remote runs held at once (running plus finished and not yet expired). When full, the oldest finished run is dropped to make room; a start is refused only when every held run is still going.

max_runs_per_token.description: Most runs one token may have going at once; finished runs do not count. A start beyond it is refused with 429 too_many_runs.

run_timeout_ms.description: Longest a message run started through the remote API may take; it is then stopped (a sub-agent run keeps its agent's own timeout_ms).

run_retention_ms.description: How long a finished remote run stays readable.

wait_max_ms.description: Longest a status request may wait for a run to end.

result_max_bytes.description: A run's answer is cut to this many bytes (UTF-8 safe) and flagged cut.

path.description: Session-root directory relative to the system setting.json parent; absolute paths are used as-is.

libraries.description: Directories read at startup, relative to the system setting.json parent.

command_dirs.description: Custom slash commands: each Markdown file is a command whose word is its path below the folder without .md, each part made a slug and the parts joined by ':' (review.md is /review, git/commit.md is /git:commit). Front matter may give description and argument-hint; the text may use $ARGUMENTS (everything typed after the word) and $1 to $9 (its words; a double-quoted run is one word), and without either the arguments follow as a new paragraph. A word found in an earlier folder hides the same word in a later one. A file whose word is a built-in command (compact, state, reset, plan) or starts with prompt:, template:, skill:, mcp: or resource: is skipped. The web client's / menu and jad run read them.

tool_definition_paths.description: Native tool definition files. Replaces the per-session tool_definition_paths.

max_asset_bytes.description: Largest prompt, template, skill or command file the library reads. A larger file is skipped.

catalogs.description: Folders of the catalogs, relative to the system setting.json parent. Each is read as <folder>/<category>/<name>.json (state is the exception: <folder>/<session>/<profile>/). The remotes folder holds <name>.json files of kind remote (other JAD servers this one may call); there is no category level. Defaults: .jad/profiles, .jad/models, .jad/tools, .jad/mcp, .jad/remotes, .jad/state.

defaults.description: Setting values every session starts from. Objects merge key by key with the level below it (profile, session); arrays and scalars replace. Each value follows the same key in setting.schema.json. This file is read once when the server starts, so a change here (defaults included) applies only after a restart; the profile and session files are read on every request.
